# requires: logging
#
# A lie is evidence, and deleting it destroys the only signal worth alerting on.
# A process claiming to be the init system while the kernel reports an ordinary
# account running an ordinary binary is the interesting case, and it is only
# expressible because both halves stayed on the record.
#
# A dispute compares claims about one subject: the writer's claim against the
# attestation about the writer, and only when that attestation stands. A relay
# carrying a different pid from the writer is expected, not a dispute (chain
# step 15), and a contradiction the receiver has no basis to trust is not one
# either -- it is an unverified author, which is a different answer.
#
# The third record is the other absence: a platform whose attester cannot
# answer. The line must say that nothing could be established rather than
# arriving unattributed for an unknown reason.
record R 0
attest R so_peercred
disputed R
record S 0
attest S so_peercred contradicts
chain S
disputed S
record T 0
attest T none
chain T
keys T
author T
record V 0
attest V so_peercred contradicts
send V
attest V so_peercred relay
disputed V
record X 0
attest X so_peercred contradicts
send X
attest X so_peercred
disputed X
author X

# expect 3: ok disputed=no [LOG-I10]
# expect 6: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:established [LOG-I4]
# expect 7: ok disputed=yes [LOG-I10]
# expect 10: ok 0:self:claimed [LOG-I12]
# expect 11: ok logging.peer_error [LOG-I12]
# expect 12: no-answer unattributed [LOG-I9]
# expect 17: ok disputed=yes [LOG-I10] [LOG-I14]
# expect 22: ok disputed=no [LOG-I10]
# expect 23: no-answer unattributed [LOG-I14]
